goals.text: 验证：神经网络的泛化行为能否作为 bootstrap 解空间刚性的探针

unknowns.text: The assumption that neural network generalization behavior directly reflects bootstrap solution space rigidity may oversimplify the relationship between model performance and theoretical stability metrics; this mapping lacks rigorous mathematical grounding in current literature.

Bootstrap resampling procedures used to estimate solution space variability may be computationally infeasible or statistically unstable when applied to high-dimensional neural network parameter spaces without proper regularization or dimensionality reduction.
There is no established benchmark dataset or ground-truth metric for “solution space rigidity” in neural networks, making validation of the proposed probe mechanism inherently circular or subjective.

The analysis may fail to account for architectural differences (e.g., CNNs vs. transformers) or training dynamics (e.g., learning rate schedules, optimizer choices) that independently affect both generalization and bootstrap-derived uncertainty estimates.

The physical analogy from condensed matter physics (e.g., phase transitions, electronic structure) used to motivate the concept of “rigidity” may not translate meaningfully to abstract function spaces in machine learning, risking misapplication of domain-specific concepts.
The assumption that neural network generalization behavior directly reflects bootstrap solution space rigidity may oversimplify the relationship between model capacity and theoretical constraints.
Training dynamics such as optimization path dependence or local minima could influence generalization independently of underlying structural rigidity.
Lack of ground-truth solutions from analytical or high-fidelity methods makes it difficult to validate whether observed generalization trends truly probe rigidity.
Boundary conditions like network width/depth extremes or noise levels might induce phase-like transitions in generalization not captured by current experimental design.
The mapping between neural function spaces and bootstrap solution manifolds lacks formal justification — architectural choices may inadvertently bias the probe.
Neural networks may not capture the underlying physical principles governing bootstrap solutions, leading to incorrect generalization behavior.
The training process might suffer from local minima, resulting in a suboptimal model that does not accurately represent the true solution space.
Insufficient or biased training data could lead to poor generalization, especially in regions of the solution space that are underrepresented.
The model might fail to generalize well at extreme values of parameters (e.g., very high or low temperatures, pressures) if such cases are not included in the training data.
The architecture of the neural network might be too simple to capture complex relationships in the bootstrap solution space, leading to oversimplification and loss of critical details.
